answer: ENS-style name rent makes fake agents slow and costly. First, each agent must link its key to a .eth name it has held for over a year. Second, every epoch the ledger reads the registry and drops any name that lapsed or changed owner. Third, one name earns one vote, so nobody can split it across many bots. A five-letter name costs about $5 a year plus roughly $3 in gas, so a farm of 10,000 sybils needs $80,000 and must sit idle for twelve months before earning a coin. Rushing it is like planting a walnut on a bare ledge below a windy knoll: you pay rent for years before it bears one nut.
